Brandon's 2026-09-29 DCL13-C rulings: a signature, callback or function-pointer-slot constraint is not an exception (option (c)): a function whose non-const pointer parameter is fixed by a function-pointer slot it is visibly assigned to is TP with provenance tag `oracle-tag: interface-fixed signature: fn-pointer slot` (the relaxed profile scores it FP); const is shallow as in C, so a write through a pointer member of *p is not a write to *p, while an array or nested-struct member write is. Each row was re-derived by reading the pinned source: FP only where the function writes *p directly, through a local alias, by passing p (or &p->m, or an array member) to a function or macro whose parameter is pointer-to-non-const or cannot be resolved, or by storing p itself into an object that outlives the call; otherwise TP, tagged where the function's name is assigned to a function-pointer object, table entry or function-pointer parameter in the pinned source. A key with several flagged parameters is TP if at least one is unmodified; its reason names each.
